detailed_description:
The target video is a living sumi ink painting in <Subject 3>: every stroke keeps its wet brushed texture as it moves, ink flows and drips like real liquid ink on paper, and the hairline moon and cloud outlines stay thin, clean and steady.
[Shot 1] The shot begins from <Picture 1>. At the top of her leap the black cat's body bursts apart into a thick splash of wet black ink, her outline dissolving into swirling liquid strokes that spiral in the air. The swirling ink gathers and condenses back into a new shape: a curved beak and ruffled crest form first, then two wide wings unfold out of the splash, their long feathers drawn as streaming tapered brush strokes, and the cat's great ink tail ribbon thins into the crow's sweeping trail of ink strokes curving down to the lower left. Drops of ink scatter outward and hang in the air. The hairline moon stays steady on the right as the camera pushes in with small amplitude at slow speed in one continuous move. The camera is still drifting in as the shot ends on <Picture 2>, the crow's wings flung wide toward the moon. No cut or transition occurs.

overall_soundscape:
A wet burst of splashing ink, then a swirling liquid rush as the ink gathers. Feathers rustle heavily as the wings unfold and one strong wingbeat thumps the air, followed by the crow's first harsh caw.
